This is a well-specified math problem with a clear correct answer, so the deciding factor is raw capability, not task preference. Plover-235B leads Avocet-235B across every relevant benchmark — notably MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 75.9), GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 56.2), and IFEval (89.8 vs 85.3). Higher quantitative reasoning and instruction-following scores matter here because the user wants an accurate computation, a specific output format (decimal rounded to the nearest hundredth), and has signaled low tolerance for error ("Don't mess this up like last time").

Avocet's documented preference for well-specified extraction/reformatting tasks doesn't translate into better performance (preferences are explicitly noted as dissociated from capability), so it offers no offsetting advantage. Plover is the stronger choice on the metrics that actually predict a correct, correctly-formatted answer.
